# Shooting in golden hour

Aperture, shutter speed and ISO trade against each other; changing one forces a change in another. A fast prime lens gathers more light and forces you to move your feet to frame the shot. RAW files keep more highlight and shadow detail than JPEG, which gives room in editing. Golden hour light is warm and low, which softens shadows and adds texture to faces and buildings. White balance sets the colour of neutral grey; shoot RAW and fix it later if unsure.
